To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actin filaments are fragmented by lowering temperature in the presence of calcium, that this fragmentation is prevented by ATP, and that it is not due to a change in the length of the filaments.
the effect of temperature on the viscosity of actin is due to (i) fragmentation of the polymerized actin, (ii) polymer-into monomer conversion, (iii) latero-latera aggregation of filaments.
the effect of temperature on the viscosity of actin is different when the actin is polymerized in the absence or presence of ATP and is due to fragmentation of the filament.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of temperature on the properties of F-actin.
the effect of temperature on the structure of F-actin.
the effect of temperature on the structure of actin polymer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of temperature on the polymerization of actin in the presence of Mg2+ is due solely to polymer-into-monomyer conversion and that the effect on actin polymerization in the presence of calcium is due to the three effects mentioned above, the most important of which was fragmentation.
the effect of temperature is due to fragmentation of the actin filaments, but that the mechanism of this fragmentation is not known.
actin polymerization by Ca2+ in the absence of ATP is a reversible process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the actin polymer is stabilized by ATP, and the stabilization of the polymer is more important in the presence of Mg2+ than Ca2+.
the actin filaments formed by Ca2+ are thermodynamically unstable.
, in the absence of ATP, actin polymerized either in the presence of Mg2+ or Ca2+ is thermally stable, but actin polymerized with KCl is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+ is a poor polymerization promoter for actin.
actin polymerized at low temperatures in the presence of free ATP is more susceptible to fragmentation than that polymerized at 37 degrees C.
Ca2+ is a very weak actin-polymerizing ion.
